supersession_rationale: Stage 3B v1 required a per-observation publication/release timestamp proven earlier than the 15:00 CST A-share close (timestamp_policy = OBSERVATION_DATE_IS_NOT_AVAILABLE_AT_RELEASE_OR_VINTAGE_TIMESTAMP_REQUIRED; unproven_release_timestamp_action = FAIL_CLOSED).
North-Star review determined this requirement conflated two distinct timing concepts: (1) the underlying Brent market observation time, and (2) a later data-distributor publication/release time.
EIA/FRED publish daily observations in batches; the batch-publication time is a distribution artifact, not evidence of when the market observation itself formed.
For a daily explanatory study the only real hazard is using Brent market changes that occurred after the A-share close on day t to explain A-share day t.
The corrected, frozen rule therefore aligns each A-share trading day t to the latest Brent observation date strictly before t and never uses the same-calendar-day overseas close.
This is a pre-outcome supersession fixed before any PetroChina result is computed; it is not a post-hoc fallback after results.
